title: Nonperturbative magnetotransport from band geometry in Weyl semimetals
abstract: We develop a nonperturbative semiclassical theory of magnetotransport in Weyl semimetals, retaining the full magnetic-field dependence of the Fermi-surface conductivity in the presence of Berry curvature and orbital magnetic moment effects. We obtain closed-form expressions valid to all orders in the magnetic field within the semiclassical regime. We show that the exact continuum formulation exhibits an intrinsic infrared sensitivity associated with the singular behavior of the orbital magnetic moment, requiring a physically motivated regularization. While the full conductivity tensor reduces to the standard quadratic magnetoconductivity, we demonstrate that magnetic-field expansion and momentum integration do not commute, leading to nonanalytic contributions at the level of scalar transport coefficients. Our results identify a regime, relevant for low carrier densities or moderate magnetic fields, where magnetotransport becomes intrinsically nonperturbative and cannot be captured by conventional weak-field expansions.
summary: This paper develops a nonperturbative semiclassical theory for magnetotransport in Weyl semimetals. It calculates the full magnetic field dependence of the conductivity tensor, demonstrating that conventional weak-field expansions are insufficient under certain conditions. The work provides exact closed-form expressions valid across various magnetic field regimes.
main_problem: To develop a nonperturbative semiclassical theory for magnetotransport in Weyl semimetals, retaining the full magnetic-field dependence of conductivity.
main_result: The authors show that magnetotransport becomes intrinsically nonperturbative at low carrier densities or moderate fields, yielding closed-form expressions and revealing nonanalytic contributions absent in weak-field expansions.
method: The study employs semiclassical chiral kinetic theory, deriving current density formulas by retaining the full magnetic field dependence of phase-space factors and generalized velocities.
model_or_system: The system is Weyl semimetals, analyzed using a low-energy Hamiltonian near each Dirac node. The physics incorporates external electromagnetic fields ($\mathbf{E}, \mathbf{B}$) coupled to emergent chiral fields ($\mathbf{E}_\chi, \mathbf{B}_\chi$) and the orbital magnetic moment.
key_observables: The conductivity tensor components ($\sigma_{ij}$), particularly the intrinsic Hall response $\sigma_{Hall}^{\chi}(B)$, are key observables.
important_parameters: Low carrier densities or moderate magnetic fields define the nonperturbative regime. The analysis is valid in the semiclassical limit, neglecting Landau quantization effects.
main_assumptions: The theory relies on semiclassical approximations and assumes that retaining the full field dependence of the equations of motion captures physics beyond weak-field expansions.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares exact nonperturbative results for $\sigma_{Hall}^{\chi}(B)$ against weak-field expansion predictions, showing deviations at moderate fields. Figure 2 illustrates Fermi-surface deformation induced by the orbital magnetic moment.
paper_structure: The paper develops the theory by first establishing the semiclassical framework using effective chiral fields. It derives closed-form expressions for intrinsic currents and then analyzes conductivity components ($\sigma_{L}^{\perp}, \sigma_{L}^{H}, \sigma_{L}^{\parallel}$) by comparing results from full field dependence versus perturbative expansions.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the rigorous treatment of nonperturbative effects in response functions (like conductivity) using semiclassical methods shares conceptual overlap with analyzing quantum responses in open or driven systems where weak-field approximations fail.
